To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a translocation of a part of the Xp chromosome with a part of the Y chromosome results in postnatal growth deficiency, developmental delay, facial dysmorphism and partial ichthyosis in the male and normal phenotype with borderline intelligence in the female.

a male with a de novo Xp22.2-->pter;Yq11.21--->qter translocation and his mother with a de novo reciprocal Xp22.22-->pter;Yp11.21-->pter translocation have a normal phenotype, except for a growth retardation, a developmental delay, a partial ichthyosis, and a facial dysmorphism in the boy and borderline intelligence in the mother.
we identified a novel Xp22.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new Xp22.2-->pter/Yq11.21 translocation in a male and his mother with clinical and genetic investigations.
the identification and characterization of genes involved in the pathophysiology of human disorders.
the clinical and molecular characterization of a patient with a balanced Xp22.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical phenotype is caused by haploinsufficiency of the Xp region.

a deletion of Xp22.32--pter in combination with gain of a small part of Yq11.22--qter is associated with growth retardation, mental retardation, partial ichthyosiform erythroderma and facial dysmorphic features in the male and borderline intelligence in the female.
a Yq11.22-->qter chromosomally balanced translocation in a female may result in a normal phenotype, but in a male may cause a severe phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Yq11-->qter chromosomel segment is not essential for normal male development, but may have a role in the pathogenesis of the phenotype of our patient.
haplo-insufficiency of Xp22. 3-->pter in the proband resulted in postnatal dwarfism, developmental delay, ichthyosis and partial facial dysmorphism.

a Yq11.1;Xp22.1 translocation in a male and his carrier mother results in a male with growth retardation, mental and physical retardation, ichthyosis and dysmorphic features and in a mother with borderline intelligence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a balanced Xp22.2/Yq11.2 translocation can cause a phenotype with postnatal growth retardations, developmental delay, facial dysmorphism and ichthyosis in a male.
the Xp22 breakpoint was located between the KAL gene (encoding for Kallmann syndrome) and the DXS278 marker, suggesting that the Kallmann syndrome is the main cause of the phenotype of the proband.
the Yq11 breakpoint in our case was located distally from the AZFb region.
